mcp: align policy matching and gallery command admission

Use the same matching rules for editor MCP servers and the Copilot runtime.
Use the install parser to check gallery commands before installation.

- Give command and URL allow entries priority over name entries for the same transport.
- Keep deny rules additive and check the final command or endpoint before execution.
- Resolve policy environment variables on the host that runs or connects to the server.
- Require explicit resolved policy values at connection start and document their use.
- Match URL schemes and hosts without case sensitivity, but keep paths case-sensitive.
- Check each gallery package or remote candidate with the shared install parser.
- Add tests for gallery admission, host expansion, startup, policy changes, and redirects.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341800
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/338879

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed await, the per-fetch caller, and the start-time cache are directly traced in repository code. The exact milliseconds depend on extension-host placement, but the added serialized boundary and request multiplicity are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: One additional extension-host RPC and policy-value object allocation per HTTP request or redirect hop, plus repeated scans of the full allow/deny policy list.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows as O(R × P), where R is the number of MCP HTTP request/redirect hops and P is the number of configured policy matcher strings; the expensive RPC occurs once per hop whenever at least one policy string references the environment, regardless of URL repetition.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased per-request latency and lower HTTP MCP throughput, especially when the executing extension host is remote.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The extension host already made one RPC to `$checkMcpServerAllowed` per HTTP destination, and the main thread checked the URL locally without another host round trip. This PR also passes the resolved policy values at server start and stores them in `_serverPolicyValues`, so request checks previously had no nested host-resolution boundary.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each `$checkMcpServerAllowed` invocation now retrieves all policy strings and, whenever any contains an environment reference, synchronously calls back into the extension host via `$resolveMcpPolicyVariables` before allowing the fetch to proceed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `await this._proxy.$resolveMcpPolicyVariables(values)` at line 242 is on `$checkMcpServerAllowed`, which `ExtHostMcp._fetch` awaits before every non-auth HTTP request and every redirect hop; the same diff stores start-time `options.policyValues` in `_serverPolicyValues` at lines 127-130.
Findings.Title: Reuse the cached policy expansion for each request
Findings.Impact: For remote MCP servers under environment-based enterprise policies, every MCP HTTP operation is delayed by an extra serialized extension-host round trip before its network request; remote extension hosts can turn this into an additional remote IPC/network latency per protocol message, reducing tool-call throughput. Redirects multiply the delay.
Findings.Evidence: `ExtHostMcp._fetch` calls and awaits `$checkMcpServerAllowed(this._id, currentUrl)` inside its redirect loop before `_fetchInternal`. The changed handler then awaits a main-thread-to-extension-host RPC whenever the enterprise policy has an environment reference. `McpServer.start` already resolves those same values through the selected connection and forwards them in `start(..., policyValues)`, and `MainThreadMcp.start` retains that object, proving the per-request RPC duplicates available state.
Findings.Recommendation: Use the policy values already stored for the server at start for request checks. If policy configuration changes, invalidate or refresh that cache once per server/policy epoch (or resolve only missing newly introduced strings), rather than calling the extension host on every fetch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse or initiate installation of an MCP gallery server under allow/deny policy
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `canInstall`/`isAllowed` synchronously parses each supported package and remote candidate before the UI admits installation; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is introduced inside the changed admission code. The later install boundaries are unchanged and outside this added parsing step.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the number of remotes plus supported NODE/PYTHON/DOCKER/NUGET packages in one gallery manifest; each candidate is parsed once and evaluation stops after the candidates have been constructed, so construction itself does not short-circuit.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely synchronous local CPU work per `isAllowed` call; separate gallery rows/actions may invoke it independently, with no queue or limiter needed because no expensive boundary is crossed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No candidate parse cache exists, so repeated action-state evaluations repeat local parsing; manifests and candidate sets are normally small, and no negative-cache or boundary retry mechanism is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that parsing/allocation was added and scales with candidate metadata; low evidence that its bounded CPU cost is material.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Gallery list size and action refresh frequency vary, but each manifest's candidate count and argument data are bounded enough that the added local parsing does not establish a user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No report: added CPU/allocation is bounded per manifest and does not introduce an expensive boundary or proven hot-path impact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start or restart a local stdio or remote HTTP MCP server with environment-dependent enterprise policy
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After connection resolution and before process/network startup, `McpServer.start` awaits host-side policy expansion, evaluates the resolved launch, then starts the transport. The new expansion RPC is therefore on the startup critical path when policy contains environment references.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve all environment-referencing policy strings on the selected extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per server start/restart when at least one allow/deny value contains an environment reference; zero when none do.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No host policy-expansion RPC occurred; policy checking was local.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before policy evaluation and before the transport can start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start a stdio server process or establish the remote HTTP MCP transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transport start per server start attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same process/transport startup occurred without the preceding policy-expansion RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing dominant startup boundary, reached only after the new policy check.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One expansion per independently starting server; policy payload scales with the deduplicated set of environment-referencing command and URL strings.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each server's `_connectionSequencer` serializes its starts, while different servers can resolve/start concurrently; there is no global expansion limiter or coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Values are not shared across servers or starts, but are retained for the lifetime of each started connection. Empty policy sets skip the RPC.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the new boundary and ordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users may start few or many servers and remote-host latency varies. One required RPC per start is a bounded correctness cost and is small relative to process/network startup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate report: the startup expansion is bounded to one per start and required to authorize against the executing host; the more serious duplication occurs on every HTTP request.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send MCP HTTP protocol requests, including redirect hops, under an environment-dependent policy
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before each network fetch and each redirect hop, the extension host awaits its existing `$checkMcpServerAllowed` RPC to the main thread. The changed main-thread handler then awaits a second RPC back to the extension host to re-expand policy strings before checking and allowing the network request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ask the main thread to authorize the current request URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing RPC per non-auth HTTP request and per redirect hop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single authorization RPC occurred before each request/hop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call back into the extension host to expand every environment-referencing policy value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One newly added nested RPC per request/redirect hop whenever the policy contains at least one environment reference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The main thread checked locally and returned without a nested host RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The main thread and original request both await it before network I/O can begin; for a remote extension host it may traverse the remote IPC channel.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform the MCP HTTP request or followed redirect.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fetch per request plus up to the redirect bound; auth retries can add existing fetches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Network fetch followed the single authorization RPC directly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Starts only after both policy RPCs complete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The added cost scales with total HTTP request and redirect-hop count, multiplied by the full policy-string scan; repeated requests to the same URL are not exempted.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within each fetch the nested RPC is strictly serialized before network I/O. Concurrent protocol requests can create concurrent nested RPCs; no shared coalescing or limiter exists.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Start-time expansions are already retained in `_serverPolicyValues`, but the request handler ignores them for resolution and refreshes/overwrites the map on every request. There is no per-policy-epoch cache or coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the changed await, request-loop caller, and existing start-time cache are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency depends on local versus remote extension-host placement and request volume; the extra serialized boundary per request is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported: this diff adds avoidable per-request IPC latency and reduces remote MCP throughput.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply an allow/deny policy change while HTTP MCP servers are active
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The configuration event synchronously walks active servers and each server's deduplicated set of previously visited URLs, performs in-memory policy matching with retained values, and sends a stop command only when a URL is no longer allowed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop an extension-host MCP transport that becomes disallowed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one stop IPC per active server found disallowed; matching breaks after the first blocked URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Policy changes already stopped active servers that failed reevaluation; the diff only supplies retained policy values to matching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only blocked servers wait for/receive cleanup; allowed servers perform local checks only.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: In-memory work scales with active HTTP server count times each server's unique visited URL count, with early exit on the first denial.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous event traversal; stop notifications are issued per blocked server without added fan-out for allowed servers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Visited URLs and per-server policy values are retained only for the connection lifetime and removed on stop/dispose. No unbounded lifetime retention was introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in lifecycle cleanup and cardinality from the maps and deletion paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Active server and unique destination counts vary, but both are connection-scoped and no new expensive boundary was added to the allowed case.
Scenarios.Verdict: No report: cleanup is present, retained state is connection-bounded, and the diff does not add an expensive boundary to routine policy-change reevaluation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 23 changed files and traced gallery admission, server startup, per-request URL enforcement, redirects, policy changes, caching, cleanup, and host/process/network boundaries. Submitted one medium-confidence-impact/high-mechanism-confidence finding for the newly nested extension-host RPC on every HTTP request; no other changed mechanism met the reporting threshold.
